facts.raw_span: A 73-year-old man presented with intractable hiccups
His past medical history included fatigue several years prior
he received chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
Serial monitoring thereafter revealed normal complete blood cell counts
The patient was afebrile with normal vital signs
Neurologic examination findings were normal except for the presence of hiccups
Brain MRI with gadolinium showed: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on light microscopy
Flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

Nodular enhancement involving cisternal segments of bilateral glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, right hypoglossal nerve, intraparenchymal ventral medullary enhancement, and extensive leptomeningeal enhancement
Follow-up showing improvement after treatment

The patient's brain MRI with gadolinium showed diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of several cranial nerves, which is consistent with leptomeningeal metastasis.

The patient's cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features and κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation, and follow-up showed improvement after treatment.
The patient presented with intractable hiccups and had enhancement of several cranial nerves, including bilateral vagus nerves, on brain MRI with gadolinium.

rationales.F03: Chemotherapy and stem cell transplant increase the risk of CNS lymphoma
rationales.F07: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement is a characteristic finding of CNS lymphoma
rationales.F08: Enhancement of cranial nerves is a characteristic finding of neurolymphomatosis
rationales.F09: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in CSF is a characteristic finding of CNS lymphoma

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid and the flow cytometry showing κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation specifically support Primary central nervous system lymphoma, which is a subtype of Central nervous system lymphoma.
